Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Agribusiness | National EXIM Bank-funded cashew factory targets 33,000-tonne annual processing capacity Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 5:02pm EXIM Bank CEO, Sylvester Adinam Mensah speaking at the commissioning ceremony on Monday ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The newly commissioned NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman has the capacity to process up to 33,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts annually, in a major boost to Ghana's efforts to expand local processing and reduce exports of the commodity in its raw state.
Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank), Sylvester Adinam Mensah, disclosed this during the commissioning of the facility by President John Dramani Mahama on Monday, November 16, 2026.
He said the factory's annual processing capacity was almost twice the total volume of cashew nuts processed locally across the country in the previous year.
“Last year, Ghana produced more than 262,000 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts. Yet only 17,000 metric tonnes were processed here at home,” he said.
Mr Mensah explained that the facility had an installed capacity of 100 metric tonnes of raw cashew nuts per day under a two-shift operation.
He said the factory was already operating close to its installed capacity and had employed nearly 1,000 people directly, while supporting another 3,000 livelihoods indirectly.
The additional jobs, he said, covered activities across the cashew value chain, including farming, aggregation, transportation, packing and loading.
“That is 4,000 livelihoods sustained in one decision to process here at home instead of shipping raw nuts abroad,” he said.
Mr Mensah said the Ghana EXIM Bank had committed approximately $12 million to support the project, including financing for modern automated processing equipment, working capital and workforce training.
He explained that more than $3 million of the funding was used to acquire the factory's automated processing equipment.
The investment, he said, was intended to strengthen Ghana's capacity to process its cashew produce locally, create employment and retain more economic value within the country.
The factory is expected to produce cashew kernels, cashew nut shell liquid and briquettes for export, while supplying cashew cakes, briquettes and roasted kernels to the domestic market.
Mr Mensah urged the company's management to scale up operations and operate at full capacity, assuring them of the bank's continued support through affordable, long-term financing.
He said the facility was consistent with the government's 24-hour economy agenda, which seeks to maximise productive capacity through extended operations, industrial expansion and job creation.
NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited, a private initiative, is an EXIM Bank-funded factory.
